For an **overnight pellet-smoker cook**, I’d choose the **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)**. It has 2,073.6 Wh of capacity and a 2,600 W inverter, giving you extra room for a long cook and campsite essentials. One estimate puts a 12-hour pellet-grill cook around **450–750 Wh**, depending on weather and how hard the grill works. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))

If you want a smaller, less expensive option for **one cook**, the **[BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** has 1,152 Wh; the source says that’s enough for one overnight cook. For a lighter campsite setup, a roughly 1,024 Wh station is estimated to cover overnight at a typical 40–60 W running draw. ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill))

Before buying, check your smoker’s **startup/igniter surge** as well as its normal draw. Pellet grills use relatively little power after ignition, unlike electric smokers with high-wattage heating elements. Keep the station dry and well away from heat, grease, and ash. ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill), [Open.Video](https://open.video/%40gearbrain/v/can-a-portable-power-station-run-a-pellet-grill))
